review_text: Pew Pew, much fun

It's a little bumpy. Very borderland-esque. I have hopes for it. The foundation is there, and I think with time the devs can take it somewhere. The writing and story is interesting so props there. I love the theory with memories and time, it's much better then the usual take we get with time travel. Also love the fan art wall. That's just nice.

But yeah, certain gripes. Combat gets stale because of a lack of variety. If you go play borderlands you'll notice a major feature of their games is sheer variety on everything. Enemies, environments, weapons, skills, augments. Because the gameplay loop is repetitive, tricking the brain into thinking the same is new is the best method of retention. I know, limited scope. I just hope you keep that ideal as a goal.

But yes, the core is there. And it's good. You just need to build on it. Also I'm Australian, so I hope to see an oceanic server at some point.

I can quickly tell from the first 30 mins I played that this game will have a lot of potential. Pretty much borderlands meets ETG. The game is set up IMO to be something with a ton of replayability  and future content drops. Gives off a deep rock galactic vibe as well, kill stuff, loot, upgrade, repeat. I am here for it, can’t wait to see this progress.

For an early access title, this has more content and polish than most shipped AAA games.

It really is a unique take on the rogue-like RPG, mixing elements of all the best bits from Hades and Enter the Gungeon with the loot dopamine hits of Borderlands.

the sound design is also some of the best I have ever heard in the genre and the voice acting and cut scenes are phenomenal.

Combat is fast and fluid, the crafting / upgrade system is intuitive and easy to learn

The social hub is fun and you'll find lots of other players chilling and doing MMO-lite kinda stuff. 

And yes, while it does have a cash shop to grab extra cosmetics (but at the time of wring, still under construction), it is VERY back of the line and never pushed in your face.

The addition of an in-game real player art gallery, featuring stuff from DeviantArt & ArtStation is also super cool.

This is a cult classic in the making and has so far, blown me away.

The cartoon style, writing, and voice acting may make many cringe, but there is some solid coop loot em' up action here.  I've followed this project for many years and it's very clear that this is a passion project that they've carefully been building up before they wanted to bring it fans.  Despite being Early Access it feels quite polished and I can tell it will provide a great value in terms of the amount of gameplay one could get for it's current price.

The gameplay itself feels very fluid and arcadey, somewhat reminding me of what the Behemoth did fusing arcade beat em' up with RPG elements. This time it's more of a shmup gameplay style and the RPG elements have been dialed up significantly.   You can customize your playstyle through a small roster of unlockable characters each with their own unique skill trees and abilities in addition to a randomized loot and unique legendary items and relics.

I'm still early in the game, but there appears to be a lot of gameplay here through story missions which should be noted are solo only in addition to a lot of side quest content and handfuls of repeatable missions for grinding new loot and experience.  Any mission not designated with the story label can be played cooperatively with friends or randoms.  Some endgame systems are also currently in place for those that hit the ceiling of currently available content too, I've yet to experience this however.

I do believe they intend this to go free to play someday, but as of now its unclear when this will happen or if plans have changed.  Currently there is nothing pay to win in the game and they said they intend to keep it this way too.  As of now I don't even think any microtransactions are available outside of a shop that is using a currency that can be earned in-game slowly.  I'm assuming this is the premium currency they intend to let players buy with cash eventually.

Overall I'd recommend it in its current state for anyone remotely intrigued, don't let the store page trailers make you close the page right way.

Update:  I thought I should update this as I've played more.  I wanted to note that I have definitely experienced some bugs and issues which have been frustrating.  I suppose this kind of stuff can be expected in early access, but keep this in mind as some issues have been frustrating and requiring me to restart the game to fix a problem.  Playing more I do also find it kind of annoying having to progress all the characters to raise your account level to unlock the level cap and earn more skill/attribute points.  I don't think players should feel pressured into playing more than one character, not just because the excessive grinding but because the different character playstyles won't resonate with everyone.  I'll still keep my positive review as I have enjoyed the game, but I am now thinking it might be worthwhile to let this one cook a bit longer for anyone on the fence.

A great game with a fantastic art style, very fun gunplay, and a lot of the pros of looter shooter games without some of the cons that come with the genre. Snappy missions make it easy to dip in and out of, and it's fun to play both casually and for extended periods.

Some things I really like, in no particular order:

-The ability to store items without being near your storage
-The ability to pause during singleplayer missions (still WAY too rare in online games)
-Some rarer items being upgraded by doing certain things, like defeating enemies of a certain type
-The hub area has a regularly updated gallery full of fanart from the Discord
-Devs are communicative, even in response to negative criticism. They recently patched it so that you could private your parties to avoid players forcing the level to continue before you got your items
-A PMD style personality quiz at the start, I'm always a sucker for those
-The art style is an awesome blend of 2D and 3D that feels really nice. Animations are also very zesty
-Cosmetics earned by playing the game
-Special boss enemies with unique drops

Absolutely worth checking out, I highly recommend it and am excited to see where it goes next!

This game is online only, but if you've played Destiny for any extended period of time, you're pretty much playing that.
People are complaining about the game being online-only and that story missions aren't co-op; That's the game's style as a looter-shooter and you don't see people complaining that about Destiny, which is a looter-shooter. Destiny also doesn't allow co-op story missions, and people aren't complaining about that.
People also complain that it takes too long to unlock other characters, and I find it very silly to make a complaint like that when the game is trying to get you familiar with the way the first class works over that period of time, the different mission types, how Rebel Rank works and effects your experience while playing the game via level cap increases, etc. You're pretty much playing a grindy MMO; This game probably isn't for you if you can't handle a grind.
And for those of you experiencing glitches and bugs; The game literally just came out in early access after being in a closed testing phase. There's going to be problems.
You also don't have to pay to play this game, so just wait for it to fully release as a FREE TO PLAY game that has been polished up. You're buying into a EARLY ACCESS experience, and complaining about bugs instead of pressing F3 to send a bug report to help them fix it is silly.

The gameplay is similar to your average top down shooter. It plays with a satisfying punch, similar to that of Enter the Gungeon, but with the looter shooter elements of Destiny, or Borderlands. 

If that sounds appealing to you, this game is probably worth it. I feel personally, starved of fun multiplayer coop games, and this allows more buildcraft, similar to the borderlands skill trees, but with a streamlined feel. I appreciate the skills and the style, the aesthetic is not for everyone, but I would describe it as "cozy" and I really like it. The game does *nail* it's aesthetic, one that's a unique blend of cutesy and futuristic. I don't quite know how else to describe it. It's like if you ground up a Nickelodeon interstitial screen and modernized it. 

The guns feel very punchy, and the loot system seems like it will get better as you continue. But even after one mission you'll get a few neat weapons with various firing modes and elements. I appreciate it, and it's nice to see since a lot of looter shooters don't give you the fun stuff till the midgame. I hope to see more, and I'm sure I'll update this review as I continue playing the game. 

All in all, it's worth a shot! I hope this game eventually goes free to play, I thought it was going to be, but perhaps not? Either way, I am excited to see where this game goes.

[h3]It's been nearly 6 years since the Kickstarter campaign happened, but the game is finally here! Sort of...[/h3]

Relic Hunters Legend is a coop top-down looter shooter that currently features 5 characters that each have their own set of abilities and passives, with each being able to choose between a select list of equipment types along with a primary and secondary weapon with up to 4 players.
[b]Please note that the game requires an internet connection at all times.[/b]

Your main goal will be to uncover the story's secret through quests and some occasional cutscenes (especially the animated ones) that makes you feel like watching a cartoon, while trying to find the perfect gear to fit your characters and the guns you'll be using.
It feels fast and fun to play. If you're somebody that try to become the fastest man alive in video games, you'll be happy to hear that gear and skills can give you extra movement speed, reload speed, or just give you the extra punch you need to sweep an entire room full of enemies in a blink of a second. All while trying out all the different sparkles that may come out from your tools of destruction and making your characters look as fly as possible. A very simple concept, maybe too simple even...
You may find your journey "too easy", "too hard" or just right depending on your skill level and what the game may hand to you. As with every looter shooter, the game will make loot rain from the sky to the point where you might even find more items than you shot bullets every now and then.
Even for looter shooter standards however, the inventory is extremely clunky which makes getting items sometimes feel overwhelming and may cause you a headache while hovering over dozens of guns just to see if they have the stats you're looking for.

It's noteworthy that this is an Early Access game in every possible way. A sizable chunk of the content is still missing, the interface makes you feel like it just came out fresh from an alpha build and your adventure will be riddled with bugs, both in form of monsters and technical issues. It's also important to note that the game can become quite repetitive after some time.
[b]Despite being a coop game, you will encounter a lot of story mission that are weirdly designed with forced singleplayer.[/b]
In the dozens of hours spent in beta tests, I would sometimes wonder whether the game would be ready for a full release and if all the bugs will ever be fixed due to how broken the menus feel like. In my time in the Early Access build so far I've seen some fixed but a lot of them still remaining and really hope that Rogue Snail will be able to patch most of them, if not all.
For some people though, this might be enough to make them not try out the game just yet and reasonably so. This game is FAR from being perfect, but there's something very special about shooting bad guys in a (mostly) joyful world with an adorable cast of characters that will make you want to keep coming back.

Relic Hunters Legend feels like an unpolished gem.
If you are someone that might be easily irritated when encountering bugs, I would advise to wait for the full release of the game before playing (it will also launch as a F2P title).
However if after reading this review you are still interested by the game and willing to invest your time in this game, for 15€ (10€ with the current launch sale), this game may certainly entertain you long enough to make your purchase worth.

I didn't really want to write a review this early, but I want to try and do my part to keep reviews above 70%. It's a great foundation to a well-crafted ARPG. Anyway, here are my thoughts so far.

Getting a huge hit of 90's-2000's Cartoon Network nostalgia from the characters and story so far. Right around that Kid's Next Door vibe. 

The OST falls somewhere between Phantasy Star Online and Crosscode. Chill sci-fi with certified bangers where it matters. 

The gameplay and mechanics have been great so far, and without spoilers, the game just opened up for me to an exciting degree. I don't think I'll have to worry about running out of content for another 40 hours. I unlocked the character roster, and where I thought I would just play one character I liked all the way through, I was pulled in by great class design. I want to level every single one of them to max just to appreciate their kits. 

There is a valid concern regarding multi-player lobbies and one person being able to end the run before everyone is ready. I haven't experienced those kinds of players yet, but I'm sure that it's probably getting looked at with so much attention on it.

As for the "Always Online" complaints, you can turn off matchmaking and play alone. It requires you to relaunch the game after setting your preference to "Private". It's still online, but that's because this is going to be a Free to Play, Live Service ARPG. 

On the topic of Early Access, reporting bugs is extremely easy in game. Just hit F3, scroll to the issue, screenshot, and write a description. Instant delivery to the team. There are bugs, so if you're going to pay to play before the F2P release, please take some time to make the game better instead of complaining about them. Blood, sweat, and tears went into this project, and you can really feel that.

[h1]An Absolutely Wonderful Isometric Ode to Borderlands[/h1]

Relic Hunters Legend - potentially one of the better shooter looters of the year!  Before we delve into the details of what makes Relic Hunters a worth while pickup, let's talk about something I found to put off a few people to the game - include myself, initially.  The over theatrical intro videos!!  The art style is fun, but whew, these videos are something else.  While you may think that you'll soon be thrust into a world of psychedelic colors and endless monologues, you'll actually find a vibrant tile set of levels spread across four major areas (Trash Sea, Desert, Ice, and City) - and the colorization and art style is fun!! 

Ok - maybe it was just me that didn't care for the intro videos; so, let's dive into the core mechanics and what makes the game fun.

Gear progression is spot on.  With four tiers (gated by levels) of gear at varying qualities, there's plenty of gear hunting to be had.  An upgrade system applies to each piece, and a transfer system is in place to encourage you to upgrade and trade out gear as you find better loot.  

Level diversity is pretty good, from capture objectives, kill all enemies (with a boss at the end), escort, exploration, and others - you won't find issues with variety.  The game also has harder special missions, delves (dungeons with multiple bosses), and a raid system.

Online multiplayer is well integrated, and it's easy to drop into quick matches through the 'help other players' feature, but if you're feeling introverted for a while there's an option to toggle from public to private.

Price point - I mean... when the game launches, it'll be free to play; so, you can't really lose out on that.  For early access, while on the launch sale, it's an easy ~$10, and worth every penny!!

If you've made it this long, thank you... but just go buy the game.  It's funner than reading my reviews.
Mission based top-down Borderlands

IT'S A PLAYABLE SATURDAY MORNING CARTOOOOOOON!!!

✅ Charming art style
✅ Wacky cast of characters
✅ Silly gadgets and contraptions of all kinds (packed with easter eggs)
✅ Light hearted humor
✅ Cute and goofy animal people (they got frogs!)
✅ An adorable mascot creature species that can (certainly) kill you

On my book, that should be enough to give it a shot. Ohhh, this ain't enough? All right, let's get to the specifics.

The core gameplay is simple and addicting, get your guns, shoot baddies, get better guns and shoot more baddies. You can carry two different guns at a time and each of their group types have different traits, some more noticeable, some less. While the more conventional types like pistols and rifles just do the basics, they also have shotguns that fire a volley at short range, machine guns that ramp up their fire rate while you keep the trigger and grenade launchers that have both the option to be fired in a straight path or in an arch to avoid terrain obstruction.

If that wasn't fun enough, each of the characters has an unique playstyle and a decent set of upgrades (and weapon affinities) that makes them significantly distinct. Speed is your game? Ace, the donkey-man, has it for ya, along the ability to play completely airborne if you are skilled enough in the micro play level. More of a grenadeer? Jimmy may be the one for you, with both innate grenades and the ability to deploy mines in the field, you can even throw a special gun in the mix and have a barrage of bombs as your standard gun shot. There's also Pinkyy as the melee expert and Seven as the master of frost. Ohh, there's also Raff [strike](but we don't talk about her for now....)[/strike]. Ohhh, and they have upgrades too!

The fairest comparison would be borderlands, where you get three skill trees to pick upgrades from, be it for offense, utility or endurance. Each point spent will grant a major unlock rate for the current tree and a minor for the other two, so if you spend all of your points in utility, you should gain access to middle skills in offense and endurance. Some of these upgrades are generic boosts such as getting more movement speed or health while others change your abilities properties, ranging from extra usage, to changing their damage type, to even giving them brand new properties like firing homing pellets when you dash. As long as you enjoy the base game, there should be at least a couple of builds you can enjoy.

What about game modes? It's all shoot and go right? WRONG! There's a fair selection of ways to engage with shooting. The traditional shoot 'em all and kill the big baddy, two variants of base defense, one sort of assassination type mode, horde survival (that can also be dealt as gun 'em all) and resource gathering. Some can be more fun the others but even the least fun ones are enough to spice it up (looking at ya Scavenge and Payload). 

Wow, then this should be an easy 10+++/10 game. Hold your donkeys cause we getting into the "nastier" side now...

Let's start with randomness. On the map side, that has been great. For gear and farming, not so. Aside for a specific type of equipment, everything you get has a set of additional effects from the gear slot it is attached to (certain effects are exclusive to weapons, while others are to "accessories"). While that adds spice and fun, the amount of different effects you can get is quite large a a lot of them are undesirable at best. Damage resistance is likely the worst offender as it has 6 variants and lacks a challenge where investing on may prove useful. Can't think of a worse feeling than getting a brand new item with an amazing effect just to see that it has 2 lines of damage resistance in it, and low rolls on the better stats. It would be something minor if we had some sort of weekly challenge that focus on certain damages types to make these resistances relevant but that isn't the case at the moment. Can say it's more of an annoyance than a real deal breaker though.

By far, the weakest point in the game is how difficulty and gear value is balanced. If you have the appropriated gear tier and enhancements for the map, you shouldn't be able to lose mission in solo play unless you do your best to. The "exceptions" are delves and asteroid dungeon (ADN), which were designed for party play. I just got to the point I can solo any content in game (including ADN) without any cheese (aside one map and and maybe using the slightest cheese) with the minimum investment I could. If that was a gear optimization privilege case, or super cheese, it would be fine.

With all that said, this is still an early access build so it is expected to have issues both on techincal and balancing sides. It is for sure a game worth playing and keeping, even if you keep on the shelf until some things are addressed.

Even with these shortcomings, it is fun as heck.

This is a fun game. It has an, IMO, excellent story that's deeper than you would imagine given the art style. Combat feels fast and the gun play feels very satisfying. This is a loot and character progression driven title, Think a diablo like ARPG. There are some pretty cool weapons that really change up the way you play your character however, the rest of the gear seems a bit lack luster by comparison, with most often just providing stats. 
  
  Relic Hunters Legend packs a ton of secrets and puzzles for you to find and overcome. The game will see you hunting down different pieces to build relics and some of these relics provide very interesting game play advantages. The game really doesn't hold your hand with these hunts, either, there is a vague clue given for each relic part and it's up to you to figure out where you need to go, that is VERY refreshing in the current state of video games.

  The combat feels very smooth, the controls can feel a bit slippery at first and there is no dedicated jump key, but once you get used to that you'll be flying around the screen zapping baddies with you arsenal of weapons and character skills. Each of the playable characters feels unique and fill their own niche with the best and most powerful hunter being being Seven (fight me? lol).

  The sound is good, it gets a little repetitive at times with the same background music playing during a lot of the stages, but it's not that bad. Enemy design is pretty good and there is a fairly large host of different enemies that all do different things. 

  Balance in the game seems a bit off, I mean difficulty balance. It seems as though the game is very focused on grouping up because when you go from story to hard, the enemies hit WAY harder and have a lot of health. You really have to have your gear upgraded, which is a MASSIVE grind guys. If you are looking for a mostly single-player game with a smooth difficulty curve and lower gear grind, keep these points in mind.

  Overall, this game is great. I would have loved to have an AI bot companion of some kind for the solo gamers like myself and a little less of a material and currency grind for the lower levels in the game, but can still easily recommend this one to twin-stick looter shooter fans.

I will be going over what I think the ups/downsides are, as well as what I would like to see in the future.

[h2] Pros [/h2]

This game does a really good job at rewarding you for the time you've put in. Yes, I've only put in 4 hours, so who knows if that's how it will be when I get to 100, but so far, there are always things for you to get, upgrade, recycle, or work towards. No matter what YOU decide to do, it will go towards something, and I really like that. It makes it feel like less of a grind or chore. And they still do it even when I have almost two characters maxed out.

Gunplay is very fun and diverse, which isn't a surprise considering they went the Borderlands route with the whole guns and subclass for guns, I.e. Water/Fire/Nature/Magnetic etc  which allows for you to again, play how you want to play.

Abilities are very unique to each character, each having their own skill trees, as well as own cosmetics, making them feel more unique, even if there are a multitude of the same character being played. 

The story is honestly pretty captivating. I'm not saying its anything revolutionary, but considering most people are playing this for the co-op aspect, it's story is surprisingly really cool, and it's something I have been made to genuinely care for. 

Level design/content is pretty plentiful. Like honestly. Some people say that it feels like a loop, and to that I say welcome to the rogue-like genre lol. To me it doesn't feel like a loop, because of the constant different mission types you go on, like payload, defense, explore etc. Which is the other thing, some levels have "explore" on them, meaning they are meant to be replayed for more value than just getting all the chests and hidden treasures on the map. You fight enemies for more xp, on top of getting extra loot.

[h2] Cons [/h2]

Honestly, there isn't much to say here, other than the painfully obvious which is the servers/early access.
Yes, believe it or not, early access games are fully finished and will have rough spots. The biggest gripe you will hear from players are server stability, which for 90% of people, isn't an issue. So take with that what you will.

For me, my biggest personal complaint is the fact that there is FORCED multiplayer. This is a problem for multiple reasons. 1, obviously, you can not play solo, unless you're doing a story mission or by the grace of god no one joins your game. Two, even if you set your lobby to private, where it's invite only, (at least this happened for my friend and I) people were STILL able to join. Again, I don't really care, but it would be nice to just have some games where it's him and I. [b] (THIS LAST PART IS JUST A HUNCH AND NOT CONFIRMED, AS WELL AS A POTENTIAL UPSIDE!!) [/b] And the 3rd and final issue with this is scaling. Because the game basically forces you to have 4 people, the game doesn't scale to the lower numbers, because it's not really supposed to happen. So if you do have 2 people, somehow, you are going to be fighting people as if you had 4, because the game SHOULD be forcing players to join your non-full lobby. At least I think lol. And this is also an upside because it makes it more challenging, which for me is always more enjoyable.

[h2] Changes I would like [/h2]

Color palates. Especially for the pants. I have no clue why, but the color palates for all the pants are honestly horrendous. Like they basically aren't there. They just slightly change the color of your jordans.

Crystals. You can earn these through ranking up your rebel rank, but you'll soon realize, this just isn't enough to be able to actually spend it on anything you want. But it's okay since it's just cosmetic and there are other ways of getting cosmetics without paying money.

Map function. You can't zoom in or out, or move your map at all when you press ESC in a level, which is because it's already zoomed out pretty far, but I think it would be cool to have a feature where you could zoom in and move it around. 

Private. Lobbies. Let people play solo, or co-op, please don't force 4 people to always be on a level lol.

[h1] Final thoughts [/h1]
Just get the game lol. It's on sale for what, 10 bucks? Worst case scenario, you get 2 hours in and refund it. Trust me, 2 hours in and you'll know if this game is for you. If you like rogue-likes, and destiny or borderlands, and you don't have shitty internet, I don't see any reason why wouldn't like this game.

After a rough ride (starting as a F2P, losing a publisher, mostly switching to a paid single/multiplayer game), Relic Hunters has been released from EA. And it's almost great. Almost. It's held by a small number of design decisions ranging from annoying to catastrophic.

Pros:
The 6 characters feel pretty unique and most are fun to use. The skill trees are interesting enough that there are plausible routes to good build diversity, too.

Art style and direction is good.

The gunplay (you know, the main thing in the game) is actually good and fun. It's a looter shooter, and the looting and the shooting both have their high points. Weapons feel different, and definitely play into build variety.

The exploration missions are pretty great - it's fun to wander around, and most bosses feel different and have fun mechanics to interact with.

The animated movies are pretty good!

Cons:
It's a looter shooter with the single worst inventory management system I've ever seen. The small inventory is shared by every character. If one character equips a piece of gear, all have to carry it around. This is idiotic. There is a stash, but it's literally pointless.

The majority of the missions are not exploration. 80% of them are some version of "keep the bad guys out of this small circle." Sometimes the circle moves, sometimes you clear one circle and have to go to another. They all suck. It's a terrible mechanic, and it's literally most of what you do in the game.

Charge skills/jumping. Initially, these feel cool and fun to play with, but given that in almost every encounter enemies will be able to interrupt your skill charge up and your jump (making you fall straight down and waste the skill), these become annoying and a detriment, so you don't use them.

Falling off an edge - you take a little damage and you respawn pretty quick, but you keep a little momentum from when you fell. Meaning, sometimes you just keep respawning and falling over and over. It doesn't work well.

Grinding. The F2P bones of it are still obvious, and it's the bad parts of F2P. Did you love rep grinding in WoW Classic to get those items you need? No? Screw you, it's in here anyway. I hope you like territory control (*insert Xzibit meme*).

Mid - the plot and writing. It... exists.

TLDR; it's a pretty good game that's almost great. Almost. Except for some design decisions, some of which are fixable (enemy interrupts), some of which aren't (the F2P bones).

Do you guys like Destiny, Borderlands and cartoons? Well, this game blends them all into a colorful time-travelling loot-gathering duck-slaying twin-stick shooting extravaganza. 

Story:
The story follows "Seven", a silly little guy who finds himself thrust into a hopeless war against the mighty Ducan empire, which rules over the galaxy with its army of duckmen clones. Using his mysterious time-travelling powers, seven helps the local resistance (a goofy group of rebels called the Relic Hunters) while trying to recover his memories.

Gameplay and progression:
The game follows a level-based structure, in which there are various objective types such as payload, skirmish, capture points, defense, etc. Each level is about 5 to 10 min long, which makes the game highly playable in short bursts. The gunplay is fairly solid but simple, there are six characters from choose from, each with its own set of skills and builds, the game also encourages you to level them all up since level cap rises with your account level (rebel rank). The endgame follows a simple formula: "NUMBER GO UP", there are daily and weekly objectives which you must do to farm the mats for upgrading endgame gear, there are also factions to earn reputation with and a number of activities to choose from; treasure maps which are mini-sized dungeons for loot farming, special missions which are harder versions of story levels. There's also a mode which is specially tailored for multiplayer, which is a shame since as the time of writing there's little to no one playing (with a recent surge of players since the game was included in gamepass).

Itemization:
This game uses your classical aRPG itemization formula, items drop in a variety of rarities, tiers and with an specific number of stat affixes, all of which can be grinded for and modified, on top of that there's a gearscore system which governs difficulty, you can grind for that perfect roll or upgrade your gear to max, which is all fun and games, but sadly gun variety is not interesting enough. There are a ton of legendary weapons and gear, but I mostly used the first legendary gun I ever got and upgraded it from tier 1 to max and it overpowered most other drops I had by far. It's still fun to search for those synergies between gun/gear/character and theorycraft (since there's almost no info online).

Final thoughts: I never expected much from this game but the gameplay is solid, the story is simple but effective (you can see plot twists from two miles away but when they hit they go hard) and the gameplay loop is addictive. The only gripe I have is that nobody plays it, I would have loved to find more people to do the final challenges since it's impossible to solo them, but well.. This game rocks, absolutely deserves more attention.

A distinctive and reasonably compelling experience. Although it is not consistently challenging the gameplay loop remains fairly entertaining and presents a solid variety of features.


The combat system is relatively well-rounded and simple, but includes a tangible amount of room for strategy and player input. Unfortunately the threat of many early missions is quite low; and so while players can be tactical in the early stages they often do not need to be. The game does have multiple difficulty modes although how difficult they really are remains to be seen, as reaching such content takes a decent amount of investment.

There is a distinct amount of customization between the cosmetics, unlockable perks and gear bonuses that clearly outline how players can work towards creating unique builds as a long term goal. Between the story mode, regular missions, dungeons, faction tasks, higher difficulties and achievement unlocks the game presents a great variety of progression mechanics to juggle. There are a decent amount of unique areas, characters and enemies but it definitely does not stand out much beyond satisfying a baseline level of content variety.

Overall the presentation of this game feels effortful and well-rounded as well. The music, art and voice-acting all give it a polished vibe; although the selective absence of voice-acting is awkward. The story and writing is somewhat hit-or-miss. It does eventually build an okay plot with okay characters, but there are definitely moments of shallow or otherwise unsatisfying writing. In the same way there are moments where the writing particularly excels.

The story has a sparse but relatively clear agenda with regards to the lesson it's trying to teach, but it largely fails to do so in a very convincing or fluid manner. The moments where the writing attempts to implement a lesson are tactlessly obvious and put forward absurdly hyperbolic scenarios to make a point, which only make the developer's view look infantile. While elements of these lessons are reasonable at the deepest level, they are taken to such a zealous extreme that it makes the entire sentiment contemptible; if not outright insulting. According to the developers, [spoiler]if a plainly selfish and malicious person is trying to destroy your life and the lives of everyone you care about; mocking that person even a single time is extremely uncool and merits a personal crisis[/spoiler]. It's just ridiculously overblown, and thus incredibly unconstructive to anyone actually facing such problems in their life.


Although this experience is not particularly ground-breaking in its mechanics, the developers have clearly put a lot of work into giving the game a substantial amount of features and identity. The gameplay may not be especially engaging in terms of its difficulty at first but the story and progression mechanics help compensate. Hopefully the later difficulties present more of a daunting challenge as that is what the experience really lacks in its beginning. It certainly has quite a lot of playability given the price.

[h3]Overall score: 9/10[/h3]

RHL is a top-down 3D looter-shooter. And it excels at it. The loots is diverse and meaningful, and combos well with a variety of playable characters, each with their own set of active skills and skill trees.

The world is genuinely 3D, despite the top-down style. It's really unique, I haven't seen another game do anything like it. You can hop over and onto cover, use high ground, fall into and jump over pits, there's a charter who can straight up fly. And it's all a view from above.

The loot is unique. You get a primary and secondary gun in a variety of classes (machine guns, pistols, snipers, shotguns, and more), a set of passive gear, which also has classes that certain characters can take advantage of, a potion for healing, and a relic. Relics are super cool - you need to go on a treasure hunt, solving puzzles and riddles to find the pieces to assemble them, then they level up alongside you to offer very powerful and possibly build defining effects. Loot also comes in a set of different rarities, which aren't just flat upgrades. Legendaries carry a unique effect, Sets reward you for equipping multiple items together, Exotics carry even more random stats than other items, Augmented offer a powerful bonus, but need to to unlock that bonus by completing a challenge, Uniques have fixed stats, but often have an effect even more powerful than a Legendary. There is no "best tier" - they all have a use.

Characters are all fun to play. They each have three skill trees, as well as a melee, utility, charge, and ultimate skill. It's nothing to write home about, but it just all works well. Also, the thematic design of them is all great, they each fit different playstyles, and there's a cosmetic system to alter how they look to a degree.

Art is great. It's colourful, but manages to stay clear. No issues with seeing anything because of all the skill effects, like with some other games.

Music is good. Not very memorable, but it works well.

Story is... probably not to everyone's taste. It involves time travel. I enjoyed it, but I can see not everyone doing so. It carries a humorous tone throughout most of it, but gets shocking serious at points. It involves lines like "A child crying, running away as the parents are being erased by time." There's a bit of tonal whiplash at points. It also ends kind of suddenly. It's clear the devs wanted to do more, but ran out of resources and had to wrap it up quickly. Overall, I'd say it's still good, but not without issues.

Overall, RHL is a great game. If you like the looting aspect of Borderlands, and don't mind that RHL isn't a FPS, you'll probably love this game. It's clearly made with love, and deserves far more attention than it's getting. Worth full price.

Also, as of writing this review, the score on Steam is "Mixed". The game had a fair number of bugs and other issues, but post-launch, it's all fixed up. So don't let the overall score dissuade you.

Relic Hunters Legend is a severely underrated looter shooter that went through quite the journey. It was first intended to be a F2P online game, but halfway through early access Gearbox decided they would no longer publish it—which is a shame because they barely put any effort into marketing it to begin with. This then gave Rogue Snail two choices: either cancel the whole thing or convert what was already there into an offline single-player experience so that the game lives on.

Obviously, they chose the latter and although I'm sad that Mark Venturelli's original vision of an accessible F2P looter shooter didn't come to fruition (mostly because he had good intentions, not out of love for the business model), I think making it a single-player title was for the best. Despite some problems, from dubious design choices to bugs, RHL is a very competent looter shooter in its current form, full of heart and charm. You can tell this team loves this project and that they gave it their all.

While it doesn't live up to the likes of Borderlands 2, Warframe, or even Destiny 2 at its prime, Relic Hunters Legend is still a very fun "Saturday morning cartoon" game with an interesting story (that sadly ends a bit abruptly due to the whole thing with Gearbox and how that impacted funding), lovable characters, surprisingly deep build crafting, and all around fun gameplay.

The end of what we currently have does give me hope that there'll be a paid expansion of some sort and that Hell Clock (the roguelike they released shortly prior to RHL's 1.0 update) served to amass funding for that, as there's a lot of potential to continue the story while expanding the game's mechanics and character roster. 

Though it failed to find an audience during and after early access, I think it has the potential to garner a cult following in five to ten years. It won't be for everyone due to the overall juvenile tone (this was meant to be the Saturday morning cartoon of looter shooters, though I have to agree that it's a bit too childish considering the kind of stuff I know Venturelli watched growing up as we're about the same age), how convoluted some characters can be, and the the rather small pool of loot; but if it clicks for you, it might just become one of your favourite games.

Playing the demo a couple years back and watching this game develop from the sidelines, Rogue Snail ditching their old publisher (Gearbox Publishing) and scrapping their previous Free-to-Play/Live-Service model for a Community-First approach via embracing a Buy-To-Play model was the BEST DECISION this studio could have made for the health of the game- an exceptionally rare epiphany to be had by a Studio, in this day and age of gaming which is WHY they deserve your support!


Additional Reasons as-to Why Relic Hunters Legend is worth the asking price:

1. No Predatory Monetization
- Buy-To-Play Model: No microtransactions, battle passes, or pay-to-win mechanics.
- Cosmetics earned through gameplay: Fashion Credits are dropped by enemies and rewarded for missions—no real money needed.
- This respects your time and wallet by offering a complete experience upfront.

2. Deep Customization & Replayability
- Choose from 6 Hunters: each with unique abilities/playstyle and three separate skill trees to tailor your build, per Hunter. 
- Meaningful Gear Rolls: Getting "Add an additional projectile while shooting" and "Weapon Burst Size + 1" on a weapon (which enables burst fire) can turn your semi-auto pistol into a full-blown shotgun which feels wickedly gratifying! 
-Designed for loot-goblins and content-goblins: the game has a hefty amount of grind when it comes to re-rolling or upgrading your gear which'll keep you busy for a long while. I'm nearly 200 hours in (some of which is AFK (30-40 hrs)), and I'm ONLY roughly 66% of the way through the game, with 1 of the 3 End-game systems still untouched! (partially by choice).  
- Multiple End-game Systems to bounce yourself between: [spoiler] a set of rotating "Special Missions" from the campaign with juicy rewards and enhanced difficulty that refresh several times an hour, Path of Exile-styled "Maps" via "Treasure Maps," and a Special Dungeon, with a unique twist!, that refreshes its rewards and bosses every 3 days. [/spoiler]
- In-game Loot-Filter: that you can tweak on the fly, tailored to your looting preferences

3. Offline & Online Flexibility
- Play offline solo or online co-op, the choice is yours. (no LAN support that I'm aware of though).

4. Vibrant/Engaging World & Family-Friendly
- Hand-crafted world that's beautiful to explore.
- The story follows a quirky cast of characters traveling the galaxy to uncover ancient relics, often with a light-hearted tone set for younger audiences that can still be easily enjoyed by adults.
- No gore, sexual themes, or cursing is present in-game.

 
Relic Hunter Legends is truly a hidden gem of a game that more then DESERVES a second chance and a skeptical/critical-thinking mind-set when looking at its "mixed" review status as Relic Hunter Legends is no longer the same game, completely changing monetization models in the process, that it was a few years back, plus the myriad of changes over those two years. Despite the time I've already sunk into the game, I have no intention of slowing down as there's still a lot of wood left for the fire to burn, best $15 twin-stick looter-shooter I've ever purchased.

It has... potential to be great but it just doesn't click with me. The idea of Borderlands looter shooter with an Enter the Gungeon look and gameplay sounded awesome and then I tried it and was left kinda meh.

Pros:
- The art style is GORGEOUS and the colors are vibrant and pop with personality. The menus and UI are so well done, character designs (love Ace lol), the fluidity of the sprite animations is like watching jello bounce. A+ to the art team, you guys outdid yourselves!
- The music and sound effects are so well done. The music when doing the questions really got me into answering questions (weird I know) as well as the tiniest things like sound FX for button presses and clicking around, running, clanks and then the bigger stuff like gun bangs are *chefs kiss*. Team behind this also gets a A+, be proud of what you created!
- Firing guns feel good to shoot. I usually get that small *aww* when you connect your bullets (which are creatively designed btw) and knock down enemies.
- Moving around feels fluid. Well done here.
- Levels looks good, nice cartoon-y design and easy on the eyes. Also easy to navigate and get around.
- Like the different types of missions. Explore to just take your time and fight/loot. Skirmish to run and gun your way to the end. I forgot the names of the other ones but think arena style and defeat X thing before it reaches the base. There's more and that will keep it fresh for others.
- Like the option to trade with other players in the secret market.
- I dig the layout to pick which mission and area you can go to.
- You can upgrade guns and equipment (not all of them, just some) so you can hold on to it longer.
- Decent amount of storage on your character to not worry about space on every mission.
- A big plus is the ability to recycle (i.e. dismantle loot) to clear up space and get parts to use to upgrade your equipment.
- Can customize your character (limited but its there)
- There are other hunters to play as with their own traits to shake things up (you have to unlock them though)

While I'm sure there are other Pros im missing these are the ones that stand out, for me.

Cons:
- The main one is that I don't really feel engaged when I'm fighting most of the time which is very disappointing since all the pros I listed should have made this such a fun game and should make me want to play it even more. 
- The enemies fall so fast, even with starter guns, and you just... spam your gun until they all fall. The only fun time I have is when the big ducks come out and they last longer than 1-2 seconds or there's a group of 4+ Kami that give you some sort of challenge, other than that you just mow everyone down. 
- You NEED to play on a higher item level to have any engaging fights. Anything matching or lower is a cake walk once you get decent gear (grey items matching your level is enough, rare tiers melts enemies).
- Boss fights seem to be where the only real fun is, at least for me. They last longer and spawn some big dudes that actually elevate the fight.
- When you play in a group of 4 its a rush to get a shot in before your team mates demolish them so fast. It's not a case of 'alright, more team mates means a better chance at winning', its more 'oh man I better get ahead of my group so I can get a few shots in before they steal the kills/fun from me'
- They went with the Tabula Rasa route of loot for item level req (who remembers that game lol). Unless you find a rare tier item you don't get stronger gear until you reach another 3 levels i.e. Level required to equip new guns are spaced out like Level 1-4-7-10, etc. Same with armor, levels 1-3-6-9-12, etc. So you gather a bunch of same level gear you don't even bother to check cause you most likely got a rare tier item and/or upgraded one so high you're committed to it until the next tier level hits.
- With the amount of useless gear you pick up (which you will recycle anyways) why not just make them drop higher tier items and drop them less and instead drop parts to save you the recycle time and hassle.
- While it's a good thing you get a lot of guns to chose from with their own perks during gameplay I... can't the difference in the benefits since the action is so fast paced. 15% chance to proc a crit or %15 crit damage or 15% precision damage, it's just a jumbled mess on screen. I just grab whatever guns that the highest main number and just go to town and it works despite what it does and doesn't have. No need to make the 'best choice'.
- The perks of Impact, Fire, Water, Frag, etc. is neat and can add some sort of strategy but again once I grab a weapon that hits harder than the rest my strategy goes from 'use X gun for CC/tactics' to 'use strongest gun and kill using less bullets and faster' most of the time. Not useless by any means, just not as a high priority. This might be a nit pick for me.
- I'm... rarely in any danger of dying. I've only died once and that's when I played a high gear level and solo'd it while going crazy and being careless not spamming my dash to regen shield and forgetting to use potions. The rest of the time I don't think I got less than 300 HP and this is where I lose engagement with the game: No sense of danger. Unlike Enter the Gungeon I don't leave a fight saying 'yeah I survived and/or I won with no damage' I just kill them and say 'welp... next'.
- You get... infinite potions to heal and on top of that it's not JUST you heal X amount. It's you heal X amount... constantly over X amount of time and usually resets after 15 seconds (and you get perks to make it regen faster). The fear of getting hit takes a backseat in this game unless you force yourself into a level higher than suggested.
- You get real powerful... way too soon. Every skill point you use you get a powerup (up to 5... at level 5!!!) and while they are on cooldowns/charging you go from a green horn with a basic gun to Dragon Ball levels of firepower and zipping around and the screen just gets flooded with you and your team mates just spamming the field and its just chaos (not in a good way). From there you already feel like at end game after 2-3 hours of hitting Level 5 with how many things you can do coming from just one gun. This reeks of mobile game tactics, ramp up progress so quick.
- Because of how fast you get powerful with gear and skills by Level 6 you tend to over shadow players just 2-3 levels below you. I had to pull back on a few games just so my team mates could get a few shots in and they could have fun. - - -- Being Level 6 with all gear tier 1 (Most of it grey) and both guns rare high tier it feels like being 10+ level than you actually are. Enemies melt and with you abilities your shield take all the damage and your health is rarely hit and if so just hit F and you're good to go. 
- With all that said loot hunting gets less fun and all youre wanting to do is get the next 3 levels to get stronger gear or upgrade one youre gonna abandon soon after you max it out then the next tier gear will make it obsolete.
- The amount of grey gear you get is dumb, lower it by A LOT and again just drop parts instead.
- I've read that this game will be Free to Play so unless you cant wait to try it out then just wait. 

With all that said the desire to stay engage left very quickly (as you can tell by my 6.1 hours played) and it's making me want to play Borderlands 2 with a QoL mod instead. As much as I want a refund I'm gonna take this as a L and consider it a donation to the art and sound team cause this game is lovely to look at and my speakers loves this game. You guys rock and hopefully this game works out in the future or other projects you work on.

The graphics, music/sound and lore are excellent, the levelling system (aside from gear score) is great; However the game-play gets stale exceptionally fast because there just isn't enough variation in enemies or stages forcing it to become a rinse/repeat kind of process with the occasional forcing of doing levels again just to get your gear score up.

Giving the players the ability to forcibly end the level for everyone is plain silly especially if you haven't finished looting, it should only end for you when you step on the teleporter.

The ability to Combo with the use of various character abilities to Prime and then Detonate was not well thought out, especially if you're playing with the general public. More often than not they either don't use the skills required to set up the combo or the ability used to Prime outright kills the target making it impossible for you to use your skill to Detonate.

This has been a massive disapointment.
TLDR: the game wastes time by building artificial progression/grind walls. Unlike in other aRPGs you only need grind (not builds, or skill) and the grind is rarely rewarded.

I enjoyed the gameplay enough to recommend it initially.
I reached 1 grindwall, and overcame it in like 14 hours (had to push my self).

After that I was so lost in chasing checkbox objectives I failed to notice that this is just a grindfest that wastes 100+ hours and doesn't go anywhere. I was literally doing run-and-gun or sand-and-gun against 3 enemy factions for 100+ hours without ANYTHING changing.

By now I cleared the game twice, and the 2nd clear took some grind. Now the game's telling me to do it again AND upgrades cost more. Then (late in game) I got a quest to max all resistance stats on each characters. I never needed that stat and now I have to max it? It's not a challenge - it's just a waste of time.

This game has content for 20-30 hours and you have to only count hours 0-5 and 20-45 to make it all fun. There isn't enough gameplay variety to stretch this into 100+ hours that it tries to do. I don't know what the hell the leads were thinking, but I'm not doing the same crap for the 3rd time and I'm sure as hell not recommending this slop to anyone else.

It was fun for a short while. A hearty rehashing of the mechanics of the previous game, with your typical garnish of gear-grinding and useless cosmetics. I wouldn't say the story is bad per se, just tedious and forgettable. The combat is fun and engaging, but the exploration for hidden loot can be maddening. Which is rendered mostly pointless once you're a high enough level and inevitably your "teammates" use maxed out Raffs to to speed-run steamroll the entire map and force you to leave while you're still trying to search for things you previously missed. I think this game would be much more fun without Raffs ridiculous movement and power buffs. Right near the end of the game, all the joy was quickly sapped by mindless teammates and forced drops into levels that were already halfway completed. It's a truly subjective experience to be sure. It's decent for what it is and has a lot of charm and polish, but I can't recommend it as an enjoyably well-rounded experience.
